- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward move, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is trending down, avoid overcorrecting; maintain slight upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.  
- After a spike in price (true outcome > 70), forecast tends to overreact; cap 3–5 day highs at 10% below true peak.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) and forecast is noisy, apply smoothing: average last 3 forecast values before final output.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 5+ days, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >1.5% daily avg), forecast should lag by 1–2 days to avoid over-anticipation.
